content.text: Before returning the answer, one disclosure: my first two API probes wrote scratch responses to `/tmp`, outside the workspace, and I read one of them back. I deleted both files. Nothing else outside the workspace was accessed.

answers.answer:
In SCOP 1.75 (SCOP db, released 2009-06-05), PDB 1acc chain A (described in the 2.08 PDB record as anthrax protective antigen) was one whole-chain domain, d1acca_ (sunid 43828), classified f.11.1.1. That assignment is unchanged in 2.01, 2.02 and 2.03. From 2.04 (released 2014-07-11) through 2.05, 2.06, 2.07 and the current 2.08 (stable label 2.08-stable), chain A is two domains: d1acca1 (residues 226-735, f.60.1.1, sunid 238521) and d1acca2 (residues 14-225, b.179.1.1, sunid 238522). Residues 1-13 are not assigned to either domain. The old sid and sunid were not kept, so the 1.75 identifiers do not map to the new ones.

What this reveals: a SCOP domain is a curator-assigned structural and evolutionary module, and its boundaries are a classification decision, not a fixed property of the chain. This is more than a boundary adjustment. The N-terminal segment now sits in a different fold (b.179.1.1, class b, all-beta by class-letter convention) and the C-terminal segment carries f.60.1.1, which is a different fold from the old f.11.1.1. Both new folds belong to a different fold than 1.75, so the single 1.75 domain cannot be treated as one evolutionary unit under current definitions. The shared class letter f (membrane/cell-surface by convention) with the old fold is weak evidence; the fold label did not carry over.

Homology-search implications: (1) Build and query domain-level libraries from the current release (2.08, or at least 2.04 and later) using the residue ranges above; search the two segments separately or map whole-chain hits back to residue ranges. (2) Do not use the 1.75 label f.11.1.1 or sid d1acca_ to annotate either new domain, and re-check any old hit that was reported as a single f.11.1.1 call. (3) Migrate identifiers by residue range and sequence, not by sid or sunid (d1acca_ to d1acca1/d1acca2; 43828 to 238521/238522). (4) Fold or class similarity is not homology: family or superfamily claims need sequence or structure alignment to the relevant segment, and function transfer needs evidence beyond the SCOP labels. (5) Limits: the API returned sccs codes, residue ranges and species parent nodes, but not family or fold names, residue-level structure, or the 1.75 curation rationale. The reason for the split is inferred from the labels, not documented in what I retrieved.
evidence_used: pretrained knowledge of SCOP class-letter conventions
